# Autogenerated reference prototype

This Astro 7 application prototypes the separately built ClickHouse reference
site using the official [`@mintlify/astro`](https://github.com/mintlify/astro)
integration and the architecture demonstrated by the
[`mintlify-astro-starter`](https://github.com/mintlify/mintlify-astro-starter).
It exports content enclosed by `AUTOGENERATED_START` and `AUTOGENERATED_END` in
the current English `docs/reference` tree. SQL statement bodies are read
directly from their version-pinned `StatementFactory` registrations instead;
the files currently materialized under `docs/reference/statements` are not an
export input for those pages. Their metadata is derived without a per-page
catalog: the registered name supplies the stable ID and title, `parent`
supplies route ancestry, the entity type and title supply a deterministic
description, and normalized SQL names and source terms supply search keywords.
Navigation labels are relative to their resolved group; a group's sole root
document is labelled `Overview`. A new source registration therefore produces
a complete page without a corresponding Markdown file or metadata entry.

`legacy-statement-routes.json` is deliberately limited to redirects for URLs
which predate these deterministic rules. It does not control page existence,
canonical routes, labels, frontmatter, keywords, or navigation, and can be
an empty schema in a clean installation with no URLs to preserve.

The exporter also reads the version-controlled `CurrentMetrics` and
`ProfileEvents` registries and the asynchronous-metric region generated from
C++ registrations. Their descriptions are rendered into the generated
`system.metrics`, `system.events`, and `system.asynchronous_metrics` pages.
Handwritten pages and handwritten content outside the markers are deliberately
excluded.

Some handwritten index pages contain autogenerated tables of contents inside
the same markers. They are navigation helpers rather than reference documents,
so `reference-navigation.json` excludes their source paths explicitly. Empty
generated regions are also omitted. This keeps artifact eligibility auditable
and stable across versions without relying on the current Mintlify navigation.

The generated artifact and rendered pages are build inputs, not repository
content. They are ignored by Git. The ClickHouse shell and search remain local,
while Mintlify owns MDX component rendering, snippet resolution, navigation
helpers, and content synchronization into Astro collections.

The exporter snapshots `docs/snippets/components` and its shared support library
into each versioned artifact. Imports from those sources are collected while the
artifact is prepared and exposed through an ephemeral component registry. Astro
therefore renders the shared React implementations directly; this project does
not maintain parallel implementations. Adding a component import to generated
reference MDX makes that component available to the resulting pages, while a
pinned version continues to use the exact component source it shipped with.

The repository-owned `reference-navigation.json` defines the reference
hierarchy independently of Mintlify. The exporter resolves its stable groups
and membership rules against the documents present in each version and embeds
the complete result in that version's artifact. The Astro preparation step
never reads `docs/reference/navigation.json`.

The preparation step still reads the current `docs/docs.json` for shared Maple
theme values and the non-reference header menus. It also copies the existing
logo, favicon, and navbar CTA into the ephemeral public directory. Those visual
inputs therefore continue to have a single source of truth under `docs` while
reference navigation is owned entirely by this project.

## Local development

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

The regular development path creates these ephemeral directories:

- `.artifacts/latest` contains the live `ReferenceDoc` prototype bundle.
- `src/generated/mintlify` contains a Mintlify-compatible `docs.json`, MDX pages,
  and snippets materialized from the bundle currently being built.
- `.mintlify` contains the Astro collection generated by `@mintlify/astro`.

Open `http://localhost:4321/docs/reference` after the development server starts.
The development server materializes only `latest`.

To exercise a release locally, create and build the duplicate `26.8` fixture
once, then build `latest` and start the multi-root preview server:

```bash
npm run export
npm run snapshot:test
npm run build
npm run preview
```

This adds `.artifacts/26.8` and `.snapshots/26.8`. The fixture does not claim to
contain historical `26.8` source. Both directories are immutable: rerunning the
snapshot command for the same version fails instead of rebuilding or replacing
it. The preview server reads live pages from `dist` and versioned pages directly
from `.snapshots`; the regular build never assembles or copies old versions.

## Export only

```bash
npm run export
```

The exporter accepts optional overrides:

```bash
node scripts/export-reference-docs.mjs \
  --docs-dir ../docs/reference \
  --snippets-dir ../docs/snippets \
  --source-root .. \
  --navigation reference-navigation.json \
  --legacy-statement-routes legacy-statement-routes.json \
  --output .artifacts/latest \
  --channel latest \
  --locale en
```

The output contains `manifest.json`, `documents.json`, `navigation.json`,
`routes.json`, `search.json`, the shared MDX snippets referenced by generated
regions, and a snapshot of the shared React component sources. Current metrics,
asynchronous metrics, and profile events are
first-class typed search records which link to stable anchors on their generated
system-table pages. The manifest
records the exact Git revision, the bundle hash, the navigation and legacy-route
source hashes, and the hash of every included document and snippet. The
bundle hash covers the resolved navigation, routes, and search records as well
as the content, so a published release cannot silently change hierarchy or
discovery metadata.

## Version and release lifecycle

`reference-navigation.json` is the source hierarchy for every channel. It uses
stable group and document identifiers, selectors for generated families, and
explicit exclusions for navigation-only source pages, so the same definition
resolves against the documents available in different ClickHouse versions.
Empty groups are omitted and newly generated members of a known family are
included automatically.

- **Latest** is the live bundle served at the clean `/docs/reference` routes.
- Concrete versions are immutable bundles served beneath
  `/docs/reference/versions/<version>`.
- The versions catalog is derived exclusively from bundles that are present.
  It has no speculative entries, publication status, or archive grouping.
- `npm run build` always prepares and builds only `.artifacts/latest` into
  `dist`. Its page-generation cost therefore stays constant as releases accrue.
- A release event runs `npm run snapshot:version -- <version>` once. It freezes
  the current `latest` artifact, builds only that version into
  `.snapshots/<version>`, and refuses to overwrite an existing snapshot.
- Production publishes `dist` as the replaceable `latest` deployment and each
  `.snapshots/<version>` directory beneath an immutable storage key. Adding a
  version updates the small versions catalog; subsequent daily builds neither
  rebuild nor copy any frozen page output.
- The next `latest` build reads that catalog entry and exposes the new selector
  option. It does not read or regenerate the version's static pages.
- The release job should run from the exact release revision so its documents,
  resolved navigation, routes, component sources, and search index are frozen
  together before the `latest` channel advances.

The release publisher and durable artifact registry remain follow-up work. The
prototype artifact already contains the hashes and channel metadata needed by
that publisher.

## Prototype boundaries

- The regular local build includes only English `latest`. `npm run snapshot:test`
  creates the duplicate `26.8` fixture used to verify version switching.
- Non-statement routes are derived from files under `docs/reference`.
  Statement routes, stable IDs, labels, descriptions, and keywords are derived
  from source registrations. Pre-generation URLs are redirect-only data in
  `legacy-statement-routes.json`; all canonical routes are published beneath
  `/docs/reference`.
- Generated MDX is validated against a small component allowlist before Astro
  sees it.
- Standard Mintlify MDX components come from `@mintlify/components`.
- ClickHouse-specific React components come directly from
  `docs/snippets/components` through the artifact-generated component registry.
- The shell matches the current Mintlify Maple layout in both color schemes and
  at the current desktop and mobile breakpoints.
- Search is a compact, lazy-loaded client index for the selected artifact.
- A generated `versions.json` manifest powers the sidebar selector. It lists
  only existing bundles, and every entry resolves pages by stable document ID.

`@mintlify/astro` 1.0 currently declares Astro 5 peer ranges. This prototype
keeps Astro 7 and enables npm's legacy peer resolver locally; the full static
build is the compatibility check until the package expands its peer range.

Localization, object-storage publication, cross-application redirects, and the
edge boundary with Mintlify remain follow-up work.
